prompt: Write a method that returns the longest word in a sentence, with the first-longest winning ties. Complete the longestWord method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: split("\\s+") breaks a sentence on runs of whitespace, and trimming first prevents a leading empty token. The 'first-longest wins' rule falls out naturally from using a strict > comparison: a later word only replaces the champion when it is strictly longer, so ties keep the earlier word. Handling the all-spaces input up front keeps the main loop simple.
hints: trim() the sentence first, and return "" right away if nothing is left.
split("\\s+") splits on one-or-more whitespace characters, so repeated spaces do not create empty words.
Track the longest word seen so far and only replace it when a word is STRICTLY longer -- that makes the first of a tie win.
